correctness.rationale: At a zero cell, the open-neighborhood weight is exactly its row sum plus column sum. An empty column forces every row sum at least two; without an empty column the total is at least n. Both candidate weights are attainable: put one 1 per column covering every row, or put one 2 per row. For n<2m equality excludes empty columns and forces every column sum to be 1, with each row occupied. For n>2m equality forces an empty column and then every row sum must be 2. At n=2m the same alternatives are exhaustive and the two feasible families can coexist. Column assignments onto the m named rows count m! S(n,m); independent rows of weight two give (n+binom(n,2))^m. The boundary overlap assigns labeled columns in pairs to the named rows, giving (2m)!/(2!)^m. Independent adjacency enumeration gave no lower-weight examples at 2x4 or 3x6 and respectively counted (U,B,overlap,union)=(14,100,6,108) and (540,9261,90,9711). The frozen checker and recorded 19-profile output were inspected, not executed; the finite checks do not replace the equality proof.
residual_risks: Counts are for labeled boards and ordinary, not perfect, Italian domination. Independent enumeration covered the two named boundary boards only.

originality.rationale: Two verified overlaps matter. Alizadeh et al., Theorem 3.4, already give the exact ordinary scalar formula for all rectangles, not just squares. More decisively, a distinct indexed Resultary record with the same displayed date states the identical labeled optimization problem and every optimizer family and count, including the boundary intersection, on the superset 1<=m<=n. This is demonstrated equivalent coverage of the entire mathematical contribution, not a title match or a comparison to perfect Italian domination. No distinct remainder within the frozen claim is established. The same displayed date and metadata do not establish who was first; this is a failure to substantiate distinct originality, not a finding of copying or a rejection based on an inaccessible paper. No repair is supported by narrowing the claim within the covered domain.
residual_risks: No priority or derivation relation is inferred from the two displayed catalog dates or their metadata. External discovery was limited and continued coverage in the 2019 scan remains unresolved, but neither is the basis of the FAIL.
